records.name: Nebius Token Factory, formerly Nebius AI Studio

plans.name: Starter Plan
plans.allowance: Usage-priced inference. New signups receive $1 in trial credit, valid for 30 days.

plans.name: Enterprise Platform
plans.allowance: Dedicated capacity and negotiated service arrangements.

billing.free_tier: $1 introductory credit lasting 30 days. Billing setup and a bank card are mandatory during onboarding.

quotas.rate_limits: Enterprise marketing lists a Starter baseline of 600 RPM and 400,000 TPM. Detailed documentation describes dynamic limits evaluated in rolling 15-minute windows: usage at least 80% raises the next limit by 20%; usage at most 50% lowers it by a factor of 1.5; maximum growth is 20 times the base allocation. Actual defaults appear in the console.
quotas.context_caps: Model-specific. Official cookbooks advertise 1M context for MiniMax-M3, Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3-Flash; authenticated catalog access is needed to establish account-specific availability and limits.

disallowed_uses: Using public serverless endpoints for production workloads that require a guaranteed processing region
restrictions.notes: Listed clients are documented integration examples, not an exhaustive legal whitelist. Public endpoints offer no stable-region guarantee. The old Token Factory terms apply only to specified customers with active reserves; most customers moved to the Nebius Services Agreement on September 28, 2026.

privacy.training_on_prompts: Nebius states that its zero-retention mode does not store or reuse requests and outputs for training. Applicability to every default configuration was not independently established.
privacy.retention: Zero retention is advertised for inference; retention of account metadata, observability records and uploaded training artifacts was not established.
privacy.regions: Public serverless endpoints are Global and may change processing location without notice. Dedicated endpoints can provide regional placement; marketing identifies EU and US deployments.

notable_models.notes: Exact API ID appears in the official OpenHands cookbook; hosted context is advertised as 1M.
Official OpenCode cookbook verifies this ID and advertises 1M hosted context. Availability is account-dependent.
Official OpenCode cookbook verifies this ID and advertises 1M hosted context. Native model-card context is 1,048,576; the exact hosted cap was not established.

records.name: Mistral AI Studio / La Plateforme

subscription_api.notes: Current subscriptions documentation says plans apply across Studio, API and Vibe. Included monthly usage is consumed first; optional prepaid PAYG extends usage. No separate subscription inference hostname was identified.

access.key_type: Workspace API key; personal or service-account-owned credentials are documented
access.kyc_or_waitlist: Education pricing requires verified student eligibility; general API identity-verification requirements were not established.

billing.free_tier: Free mode provides limited access to Studio and Vibe. A precise API request/token/usage-value allowance was not verified.

quotas.rate_limits: Completion limits are per model and organization, measured in tokens per minute and requests per second; actual values are shown in Admin API Limits. Audio and OCR have separate limits.
quotas.context_caps: Model-specific. Current cards label Codestral 128k, embeddings 8k, GLM-5.3 1M, and deprecated Devstral 2 256k.

restrictions.notes: Service accounts explicitly support machine-to-machine workloads and workflow workers. Published subscription usage is shared across API, Studio and Vibe Code; this is not documented as a coding-client-only allowance. A comprehensive current prohibited-use list was not verified.

privacy.training_on_prompts: Studio/API data may participate in improvement programs. An Admin Privacy toggle under Anonymous improvement data allows opting out. The API toggle is separate from the Vibe toggle.
privacy.retention: With approved ZDR, eligible stateless request inputs and outputs are retained only as needed to return the response. Default non-ZDR retention duration was not verified.
privacy.regions: Global endpoint has no committed inference geography. Optional api.eu.mistral.ai and api.us.mistral.ai endpoints select regional inference. Regional inference does not make all account, billing and control-plane metadata regional.

notable_models.notes: Mistral hosts this third-party model without Mistral modifications. Card advertises 1M context and 128k maximum output.
Current Premier model for code completion and FIM; card labels context 128k.
Deprecated May 22, 2026. Official card directs new integrations to Mistral Medium 3.5; advertised context is 256k.
Code embedding API; card labels context 8k and price $0.15 per million tokens.
Embedding API; card labels context 8k and price $0.10 per million tokens.

records.name: OpenRouter

access.key_type: OpenRouter inference API key; management keys are separate administrative credentials; BYOK provider credentials are optional

plans.name: Free
plans.allowance: :free models: 50 requests per UTC day below the paid-credit threshold; official tutorial says purchasing $10 once raises the ceiling to 1,000 requests/day.

plans.name: Standard Pay-as-you-go
plans.allowance: Prepaid USD credits; provider inference rates passed through. Credit purchases carry a 5.5% platform fee.

plans.name: Business Pay-as-you-go
plans.allowance: Usage-priced access; pricing page lists an 8% platform fee.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.allowance: Negotiated fees and allowances; invoicing and credit lines are available.

billing.free_tier: :free model variants have zero token price but request limits. The official tutorial documents 20 RPM, 50/day initially, and 1,000/day after a $10 credit purchase. Paid fallbacks and paid features can incur charges.

quotas.rate_limits: Official tutorial: :free variants 20 RPM, 50/day or 1,000/day depending on purchased credits. Paid-model limits generally pass through from providers; DDoS protection also applies. Current limits reference describes a higher-tier threshold granted one credit below the nominal threshold to accommodate fees/rounding.
quotas.concurrency: No universal numeric concurrency cap verified. Certain prepaid accounts have an in-flight estimated-spend budget that can reject concurrent paid requests with HTTP 402 even while their balance is positive.
quotas.context_caps: Model- and provider-specific. Catalog context_length and top_provider.context_length can differ; free endpoints can have smaller contexts than paid equivalents.

restrictions.notes: Provider routing supports order, allow_fallbacks, require_parameters, only, ignore, quantizations, sort, max_price, preferred_min_throughput and preferred_max_latency. Defaults include allow_fallbacks=true, require_parameters=false and data_collection=allow. Set provider.zdr=true for eligible ZDR inference endpoints and data_collection=deny to exclude collecting providers. No comprehensive current prohibited-use or resale policy was established.

privacy.training_on_prompts: OpenRouter does not log prompt/response content by default; providers have separate policies. data_collection=deny excludes providers that collect user data. Policy labels represent OpenRouter's best knowledge rather than definitive third-party policy authority.
privacy.retention: OpenRouter retains request metadata; content logging is opt-in. Provider retention varies. Optional response caching stores content for its TTL; account-level ZDR disables caching, but per-request provider.zdr alone does not.
privacy.regions: Current pricing and routing reference list EU and US in-region routing for Business and Enterprise, using eu.openrouter.ai and us.openrouter.ai. An older sovereign-AI guide describes EU routing as enterprise-by-request.

notable_models.notes: Current catalog includes the model; refusal tuning and abliteration are not established.
Supports text, image and video inputs. Captured catalog listed top_provider.context_length as 524,288 despite model context_length of 1,048,576.
Multimodal model. Provider-specific output limits must be checked separately.

records.notes: The model-list API reference marks bearer authorization required, but the public catalog URL returned data through an unauthenticated web open; the conflicting authentication field remains null. Pricing and routing docs list Business/Enterprise EU and US routing, whereas the sovereign-AI guide describes a narrower enterprise-by-request EU offering. Current BYOK pricing uses $25,000/month of list-price inference without fees, followed by a 5% fee; older request-count allowances should not be assumed. The free-limit reference's numeric table was incomplete in extraction, so numeric caps are supported by the official tutorial. Model moderation metadata is not evidence of low-refusal training or abliteration.

records.name: Hugging Face Inference Providers

other_protocols: Hugging Face task APIs through InferenceClient and provider-specific routes, including https://router.huggingface.co/hf-inference/models/{model_id}

subscription_api.notes: PRO and organization included credits apply to routed requests on the same gateway. There is no separate subscription inference endpoint. Included credits do not apply when using a custom provider key.

access.key_type: Hugging Face user access token with Make calls to Inference Providers permission; fine-grained tokens are documented

plans.name: Free account
plans.allowance: No included monthly credits according to the currently opened pricing page.

plans.name: PRO
plans.allowance: $2/month in general-purpose Hugging Face compute credits, shared with other eligible compute services.

plans.name: Team
plans.allowance: $2/month per seat in general-purpose compute credits; organization credits are pooled.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.allowance: $2/month per seat in general-purpose compute credits; organization credits are pooled.

billing.free_tier: Current opened documentation says free accounts receive no monthly credits and must purchase credits or upgrade. Search-indexed official text still reports $0.10/month, subject to change.

quotas.context_caps: Model- and provider-dependent. GET /v1/models exposes provider context, price and performance information when available; native model-card limits do not guarantee every provider exposes the same cap.

restrictions.notes: The /v1 OpenAI-compatible endpoint is documented for chat completion tasks only. Embeddings, image/video generation and speech tasks use Hugging Face inference clients or task/provider routes. Default routing selects the fastest provider; :cheapest, :preferred and explicit :provider suffixes are documented. Provider-specific terms still need checking.

privacy.training_on_prompts: Hugging Face says it does not store user data for training when routing inference. External providers have their own policies.
privacy.retention: Hugging Face does not store routed request bodies or responses. Debugging logs are retained for up to 30 days without user data or tokens. Provider retention is separate.

notable_models.notes: Chat-completion documentation demonstrates zai-org/GLM-5.3:baseten. Model page lists multiple inference providers; exact hosted context varies.
Official model page lists Inference Providers, including Novita. Exact router/provider cap was not established.
Official model page lists Together AI and additional providers. Native context is 1,048,576; per-provider exposed cap was not established.
Official page lists Featherless AI inference. Native context is 262,144, but provider-specific cap was not verified.
Official model page lists Featherless AI. Older cognitivecomputations model-card URL redirects here. Uncensored tuning is documented; abliteration is not.

Official feature-extraction documentation recommends this embedding model. Model card documents a 512-token maximum and HF Inference availability. Use task APIs rather than the chat-only /v1 endpoint.

records.notes: PRO credits are dollar usage-value credits, not unlimited requests or a fixed token allowance, and are shared with eligible Endpoints, Spaces and Jobs usage. Continued usage requires purchased credits; custom provider keys bill the provider directly and bypass included HF credits. Current opened pricing supersedes the conflicting $0.10 indexed extract. Hugging Face's routing-layer no-content-storage policy does not establish provider-wide ZDR or regional residency. Listed modalities describe the broader Inference Providers service, not capabilities of the chat-only /v1 route.

open_questions: What are NVIDIA API Catalog's current universal signup-credit grant, credit expiry/reset terms, numerical rate limits and model-list authentication requirement? Historical staff answers and community reports do not establish October 2026 entitlements.
What are the unambiguous current Mistral Pro price and per-plan API usage-value allowances? The pricing extraction exposes overlapping Pro/Education variants and unlabeled Team amounts.
Does Mistral's current default API training toggle differ by plan, and what is non-ZDR API content/log retention?
Does DeepSeek offer an API-specific no-training agreement or ZDR option, and what are prompt/log/cache retention periods beyond stateless response objects and file storage?
Does OpenRouter officially require authentication for GET /api/v1/models? The current reference says required, while the public catalog was readable without supplied credentials.
How should OpenRouter's newer Business/Enterprise EU/US residency offering be reconciled with its narrower enterprise-by-request sovereign-AI guide?
Has Hugging Face fully retired the $0.10 free monthly credit? The opened pricing page says no free credits, while live indexed official text still contains the older amount.
What provider-specific caps and privacy terms apply to each selected Hugging Face and OpenRouter route? Native model context and gateway-wide policies do not establish endpoint-specific guarantees.

Can current authenticated Nebius and NVIDIA catalogs verify the remaining requested model IDs, including Qwen3-Coder-Next, Hermes-4, Dolphin Venice, embeddings and rerankers, without treating model-card presence as proof of hosted availability?

No examined official model card established actual refusal-direction removal for Hermes 4 or Dolphin Venice. Is there a separate official technical report documenting abliteration for either exact checkpoint?
